attributes.scope: First production use of tools/gdl/structdraft.py (tool.structdraft.20260831T010036Z.32af7b6f), on game/movie/movieplayer.c, 2026-08-31. Findings are about the TOOL, not the TU; the TU result is claim.moviestate-record-layout.20260831.v1.

subject: project:gdl
value: structdraft.py earned its keep on first production use -- the offset/width/site table and the per-cluster example lines replaced what would have been an hour of hand-grepping, and its refuse-to-name discipline was correct in every instance -- but four defects matter enough to fix before the next worker relies on it. (1) NOT IDEMPOTENT, and it FABRICATES on its own output. Re-running structdraft on a TU it has already helped convert parses `offsetof(MovieState, fd)` as the literal offset 0x0, collapsing all 55 converted sites in the `movie` cluster into a single bogus `unk0000` field with '55x' evidence and emitting a confident one-field draft struct. This is worse than a stale report: a worker handed that draft would 'discover' a nonexistent record. It also means the tool cannot measure its own progress -- the site count stayed at 165 across a pass that converted 111 of them, while gdlmem's own debt census correctly moved bare_sites 131 -> 20. FIX: skip or separately bucket any site whose displacement is already an offsetof() expression, and report converted-vs-raw counts. (2) THE MULTI-RECORD WARNING DID NOT FIRE ON A GENUINE MULTI-RECORD CLUSTER. The tool's own registered constraints promise a 'MULTI-RECORD CLUSTER' warning routing the user to --by-function. The `param_1` cluster merged fn_800DACD8's param_1 (the 0x1D0-byte movie record) with fn_800D967C's param_1 (the decoder object, where +32 is a vtable, not a movie field) and emitted no warning -- the two records share a variable NAME and nothing else. Only reading the callers caught it. FIX: warn whenever one base name spans functions with disjoint offset sets, which is exactly this signature. (3) THE NAMING BAR IS MISCALIBRATED FOR PARTIAL VIEWS. It requires an exact record-SIZE match, so a cluster observing 5 of a 0x34-byte record's fields can never be named. In the `dst` cluster it scored MovieBitmapHeader at hit=5/5, wrongw=0, confidence 1.00 -- correct, as the conversion later proved -- and then refused to name it because the observed span was 0x18 rather than 0x34. Every single cluster in this TU hit that wall, so the tool named nothing anywhere despite ranking the right answer first four times. Refusing to INVENT is right; refusing to ADOPT a zero-width-conflict full-hit candidate that is already an accepted file-local type in the same file is over-conservative. FIX: allow naming when the observed offsets are a subset of a candidate with zero width conflicts, and mark it 'partial view' rather than suppressing it. (4) IT MISSES AN AVAILABLE SIZE ORACLE. Every cluster reported 'record size UNKNOWN'. The true size was sitting in the same TU as a literal argument -- PlayVQMovie's `__construct_new_array(movie, ctor, dtor, 464, 1)`, corroborated by `AllocHiMem(472)` = 464 + the new[] cookie. FIX: scan for allocation and array-construction call sites on the cluster's base and offer their size arguments as size candidates; this is the difference between 'size UNKNOWN' and a hard 0x1D0. Separately, a defect in the DOWNSTREAM tool that structdraft feeds: defake_rewrite.py rewrites inside C COMMENTS. It twice planned rewrites on lines that were prose inside the very comment documenting the struct, because the comment quoted the raw form it was explaining. No harm here (the offsets happened to be unmapped at the time, and the second was defused by rewording), but a worker who documents a conversion using the pattern being converted will silently corrupt their own documentation. FIX: strip comments and string literals before matching. Finally, a WORKFLOW note that generalizes beyond these tools: structdraft cannot check a layout, only propose one. Compiling a throwaway host-gcc replica of the drafted struct and asserting every sizeof/offsetof against the observed displacements took two minutes and immediately caught a real error -- the pre-existing MovieDTextOuter typedef's `_24[2]` puts its ownsAlloc at 0x2C, not the 0x30 its comment claims, so embedding it would have shifted every field after 0x150 by four bytes and produced a plausible-looking, silently-wrong record. Neither structdraft nor defake_gate would have caught that: the gate only proves the CURRENT source is byte-neutral, and a wrong-but-unused padding claim gates green, which is precisely the failure mode claim.law.swap-loop-is-record-layout-ground-truth warns about. Recommend the host-replica offset check become a standard step between structdraft and the first defake_rewrite batch.
